newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: High liquidity keeps Manila call loan rate steady.
newsitem.headline: High liquidity keeps Manila call loan rate steady.

text.p: The Philippine interbank call loan average rate was unchanged at 10.53125 percent on Friday due to excess funds in the system, dealers said.
"The Central Bank tried to mop up liquidity by offering five-day reverse repos at a yield of 10.625 percent but there were hardly takers," said one trader in a foreign bank.
Done rates narrowed further between 10.625 to 10.53125 percent.
Volume was slightly up at 8.948 billion pesos from the previous 8.413 billion. Lenders swamped borrowers 27 to 16.
"Several banks invested in short-term government securities in the secondary market so they could earn interest on their excess cash," said one trader.
A Reuter survey of seven banks showed three-month bills were bid between 10.65 to 10.725 percent, and offered at 10.575 to 10.625 percent.
Six-month bills were bidded at 11.075 to 11.2 and offered at 11 to 11.1 percent while one-year bills were bidded at 11.515 to 11.6 percent and offered at 11.45 to 11.5 percent.
Traders said they expected rates to remain sideways next week due to more maturities of treasury bills.
